label: September 1916
headline: Thiepval Falls
deck: The Somme's strongest fortress village is taken; Bulgaria strikes Romania
caption: Infantry pick their way through the ruins of the château at Thiepval
body: On 26 September British troops attack Thiepval, on the high ground north of the Albert road, which has defied every assault since the first day of the battle. Its cellars and the Schwaben Redoubt behind it are cleared in three days of close fighting; tanks help, then stick in the craters.
To the south, on the same day, British and French troops meet in Combles, which the Germans have slipped out of in the night; to the west the Canadians hold Courcelette, taken on 15 September.

In the Dobruja, Bulgarian and German troops under Mackensen take the Romanian Danube fortress of Turtucaia on 6 September with more than 25,000 prisoners, and push north towards the railway to Constanța. Romania's armies in Transylvania must send help south.
briefs: Two more Zeppelins are brought down over Essex on 23 to 24 September
Italy opens a seventh battle on the Isonzo
Serbian troops storm Kajmakčalan on the Macedonian front
